stories.title: SpaceX Closes Its Acquisition of AI Coding Startup Cursor
stories.summary: SpaceX has officially completed its acquisition of Cursor, the AI coding-assistant startup, according to reporting from TechCrunch and Engadget. The deal brings a widely used AI software-development tool under the aerospace company's roof. Neither outlet's headline detailed the financial terms or integration plans.
stories.whyItMatters: An aerospace and satellite company absorbing a leading AI coding tool is an unusual consolidation move that underscores how central AI-assisted software development has become across industries, not just inside traditional tech giants.
whatToWatch: How Cursor's product, team, and roadmap get folded into SpaceX
Whether Cursor keeps serving customers outside SpaceX or goes proprietary
Developer community reaction to the ownership change
questions: What does SpaceX plan to do with Cursor's technology and existing customer base?
Will Cursor remain available as a standalone product?

stories.title: ChatGPT's New 'Computer History' Feature Tracks Clicks and Keystrokes
stories.summary: The Verge reports that ChatGPT now has a 'Computer History' capability that logs users' clicks and keystrokes. The report frames this as a notable and somewhat surprising level of activity tracking built into the assistant. Specifics on retention, scope, or user controls beyond what's in the headline aren't detailed in the available source.
stories.whyItMatters: As AI assistants push toward operating computers on users' behalf, this kind of tracking raises fresh privacy and consent questions that will likely follow other 'agentic' AI products too.
whatToWatch: Whether OpenAI publishes clearer details on what's logged and for how long
Any opt-out or deletion controls OpenAI adds in response

questions: What exactly is retained, and can users delete or disable this history?
